705447.t: From Proto-Hellenic *erutʰrós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rudʰrós (“red”), from the root *h₁rewdʰ-. Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀬𐀲𐀨 (e-ru-ta-ra).

705495.t: Some suggest that this form comes from the original imperative *ἔσθι (*ésthi) of ἔδω (édō), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ed- (“to eat”).

705453.t: Disputed. * Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ergʰ- (“to move, go”), cognate with ὀρχέομαι (orkhéomai), Albanian erdha (“I came”), Old Irish regaid (“will go”, future of téit), Sanskrit ऋघायति (ṛghāyáti, “to be passionate”). * Alternatively, from…

705441.t: Substantivized verbal adjective of ἕρπω (hérpō). Compare Latin serpēns and Sanskrit सर्प (sarpá, “snake, serpent”).

705442.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sérpeti. Cognates include Sanskrit सर्पति (sarpati, “to glide, crawl”), and Latin serpō (“to creep, crawl”).

705429.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *h₁er-, with cognates including Latin ariēs (“ram”), Old Irish heirp, erb (“kid”), and Lithuanian ė́ras (“lamb”), but more likely of substrate origin (along with the Latin and Old Irish) in view of the strange suffixes…

705410.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewg- (“to belch, roar”). Cognates include Latin ērūgō, Old Armenian ործամ (orcam), Lithuanian riaugėti, Russian рыга́ть (rygátʹ), Old English rocettan and Albanian regj.

705427.t: Unknown. According to Vasmer a cognate to Sanskrit ऋ॒ति (ṛtí, “assault”) and Proto-Germanic *ernustuz (“struggle, fight”).

705459.t: Related to ἐρεείνω (ereeínō, “to ask”), ἔρομαι (éromai, “to ask”) (which it replaced in Attic), ἐρευνάω (ereunáō, “to search, inquire”), of uncertain origin.

705411.t: From ἔρομαι (éromai). Akin to Old Norse raun (“trial, experience”).

705415.t: Disputed. Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *erewō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rew- (“to ask, inquire”), which is probably related to Icelandic raun (“trial, test”).

705400.t: Unknown, but possibly related to ἔρις (éris, “strife”).

705451.t: Possibly Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewH- (“to tear, dig, burrow, gather”) (Latin rudens (“ship's sail”)), or related to ῥυμός (rhumós, “pole”), ῥυμουλκέω (rhumoulkéō, “to pull a towing rope”).

705405.t: Of uncertain relation outside of Greek. Sometimes compared to Latin ridica (“vine-prop, stake”), but De Vaan finds this connection shaky at best.

705428.t: From ἔριφος (ériphos, “young goat, kid”) + -ιον (-ion, diminutive suffix).

705492.t: Nominal derivative of ἕννυμι (hénnumi, “to get dressed”).

705450.t: The stem of this word is also found in ἐρύσιμον (erúsimon, “hedge-mustard”) and ἐρυσίπελας (erusípelas, “erysipelas”).

705425.t: No etymology. Being in the same semantic field of δοῦλος (doûlos), Beekes does not dismiss a Pre-Greek, in view, also, of the suffix -ιθ- (-īth-).

705444.t: From the root of ἐρυθαίνω (eruthaínō, “to dye red, make blush”) and ἔρευθος (éreuthos, “redness, flush”) + -μα (-ma). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ- (“red”).

705412.t: According to Beekes, a denominative from *ἐρεϝ-(ε)ν- (*erew-(e)n-), a noun itself derived from earlier *ἐρεϝω (*erewō), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rew-.
